status.en: 20 armed incidents reported in the past seven days, 18% more than the week before, most of them in Mogadishu, Baidoa and Puntland.
status.nb: 20 væpnede hendelser meldt de siste sju dagene, 18 prosent flere enn uken før, flest i Mogadishu, Baidoa og Puntland.

summary.en: Somali army convoys continue to be ambushed by al-Shabaab near Baidoa, while al-Shabaab suffered heavy losses in Operation Banooda and a Bay operation that reportedly killed 75 fighters. Fitgharan forces now control the Mogadishu-Baidoa corridor and Laftagareen forces have seized Buurhakaba and a town in Bay, extending combat in the south. Ethiopia has withdrawn over 3,000 troops and will not intervene in the South West State conflict. US forces have been accused of weaponising floods by trapping women and children in the path of El Niño. The conflict caused 2,284 battle-related deaths in 2024, according to UCDP.
summary.nb: Somaliske hærkonvoier blir fortsatt ambushert av al-Shabaab nær Baidoa, mens al-Shabaab led store tap i Operasjon Banooda og en Bay-operasjon som ifølge rapporter drepte 75 krigere. Fitgharan-styrkene kontrollerer nå korridoren Mogadishu-Baidoa og Laftagareen-styrkene har erobret Buurhakaba og en by i Bay, og utvider kampene i sør. Etiopia har trukket tilbake over 3 000 soldater og vil ikke gripe inn i konflikten i South West State. Amerikanske styrker er blitt anklaget for å våpenisere flommer ved å fange kvinner og barn i El Niños bane. Konflikten forårsaket 2 284 dødsfall i kamp i 2024, ifølge UCDP.

background.title: Somali Civil War (2009–present)
background.extract: The ongoing phase of the Somali Civil War began in 2009 and is concentrated in southern and central Somalia, primarily between the forces of the Federal Government of Somalia (FGS), assisted by African Union peacekeeping forces, and the Islamist militant group al-Shabaab, which pledged allegiance to al-Qaeda in 2012.
